paragraphs: As of Friday, October 9, before the U.S. open, Nasdaq faces a more fragile setup after Thursday's sharp reversal in AI and semiconductor shares. The Nasdaq Composite fell 1.25% to 27,193.34, while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index declined 3.4%. The selloff raised questions about AI monetization, infrastructure financing and whether strong capital spending will translate into sustainable returns.

Long Treasury yields remain restrictive, even after a well-received 30-year auction provided some relief. Brent crude stayed elevated amid Strait of Hormuz shipping risks and Gulf production disruptions. Strong structural AI demand remains a supportive force, but the combination of weaker semiconductor breadth, oil-driven inflation risk and expensive financing leaves Nasdaq vulnerable to further consolidation.

catalysts.title: University of Michigan consumer sentiment and inflation expectations — 10:00 AM ET
catalysts.detail: A renewed increase in household inflation expectations could push Treasury yields higher and weigh on technology valuations; stabilization would support a more constructive interpretation of the Fed outlook.

catalysts.title: AI revenue scrutiny and semiconductor leadership — throughout the session
catalysts.detail: Thursday's sharp SOX decline puts the market's confidence in AI monetization and capital spending under scrutiny. Watch whether semiconductor participation recovers broadly or selling continues across AI suppliers.

catalysts.title: Strait of Hormuz and Gulf energy supply — ongoing
catalysts.detail: Oil supply disruptions could lift inflation expectations and long-term yields, raising the valuation headwind for Nasdaq.

catalysts.title: Treasury yields and Fed repricing — throughout the session
catalysts.detail: A stable 10-year yield would help semiconductor stocks recover; renewed long-end pressure alongside weak breadth would raise consolidation risk.

watchIntoOpen: What I’d watch into the open: a constructive recovery requires oil and long Treasury yields to remain contained while semiconductor leadership broadens beyond a handful of mega-caps. The downside case is renewed oil and yield pressure accompanied by persistent SOX underperformance. The response to favorable AI news will be particularly important in distinguishing a positioning reset from a deeper loss of confidence.
keyTimes: The U.S. cash market opens at 9:30 AM ET. The preliminary University of Michigan consumer sentiment and inflation-expectations release is scheduled for 10:00 AM ET. Oil, Treasury yields and semiconductor breadth remain important throughout the session.
sources: Reuters — October 9 oil and geopolitical developments
